thread:
Maya Luo: Quick sync on Playground streaming UI tweaks — screenshot + short clip: https://img.redwood.dev/plays/stream-ux-v2.mp4. Two main topics: (A) where to place Stop vs Regenerate while streaming, (B) how the token counter should behave when inserting prompts from the library. Also flagging dark-mode contrast on the token pill.

Ryan Chen: Strong opinion: Stop should be the more visible control during an active stream. Swap the order so Stop is left of Regenerate, give Stop a solid destructive style (deep red) and keep Regenerate outline/secondary. Keep Regenerate hotkey (Ctrl/Cmd+Enter), add Stop shortcut (Esc).

Jules Park: Accessibility points: announce streaming start/stop via an aria-live polite message like: "Assistant is streaming" / "Assistant stopped streaming". Stop needs an aria-label like "Stop streaming response". Token counter should expose a readable label such as "Token estimate: 42, updating" and switch to "Tokens: 42" when final.

Samira K.: Repro for a token counter inconsistency: pick a prompt from the prompt library (I used `quarterly_pitch`), insert -> generate -> hit Stop mid-stream. The counter often stays at the prior estimate. Fix options: show a live updating estimate during stream and then transition to final value, or disable/grey the counter while streaming to avoid confusion. I prefer showing an updating estimate plus a small transition badge that flips to the final count on completion.

Kevin O.: Tab order issue: keyboard navigation currently focuses the prompt library button before Stop/Regenerate, which is annoying. Tab should hit Stop then Regenerate then prompt library. When a prompt is inserted and triggers run, focus should move to the composer input so keyboard users can immediately edit. Mobile: make Stop at least 44x44 touch target.

Maya Luo: Copy proposals: Stop button label = "Stop" with tooltip "Stop generation — Esc"; Regenerate tooltip = "Regenerate — Ctrl/Cmd+Enter". Token pill copy: while streaming show "Tokens: 42 (est.)" then collapse to "Tokens: 42" once final.

Jules Park: For the token element use `role=\"status\"` and `aria-live=\"polite\"`. If we grey it during streaming, update the accessible text to "Token estimate updating" so SR users know why the number is changing.

Samira K.: Contrast details: token pill text `#5b6a77` on `#0f1720` fails AA in dark. Recommend text `#d1e6ff` on `#1b2430` or bump weight to semibold. Stop button red should be `#d6454a` rather than `#ff6b6b` for adequate contrast with white.

Maya Luo: Prototype CSS suggestion:
```
.token-pill {
  background: var(--bg-elevated);
  color: var(--text-strong);
  padding: 4px 8px;
  border-radius: 999px;
  font-weight: 600;
}
.btn-stop { background: #d6454a; color: #fff; }
```
Will iterate on tokens and color tokens.

Ryan Chen: UX microcopy idea: change prompt library action from "Insert" to "Add to composer" — clearer. If user inserts while a generation is running, show a brief inline toast: "Prompt queued — will run after current generation" with an action "Run now (cancel current)". Should the default be queue or cancel? Product decision.

Maya Luo: My vote is queue by default (non-disruptive), but include "Run now (cancel)" for power users. The toast should be actionable.

Kevin O.: Toast accessibility: non-modal but should be reachable via keyboard. `Enter` should trigger "Run now" and `Esc` should dismiss the toast. Toast content must be announced via `aria-live`.

deploy-bot: Preview deployed at https://preview.redwood.dev/boards/streaming-ux/129 (build 9907).

ui-test-bot: A11y smoke: token counter contrast fails in dark mode (WCAG AA). Report: https://ci.redwood.dev/a11y/9907/report.

Maya Luo: I'll file a small PR addressing: button order + shortcuts, aria-live for streaming and tokens, and color contrast fixes. Will also update token behavior to show live estimate and flip to final on stop/complete.

Ryan Chen: Implementation note: Stop must be idempotent — clicking it when nothing is streaming should be a noop.

Jules Park: +1 for ARIA updates.

Samira K.: +1, I'll review the color patches.

Kevin O.: I'll add keyboard-focused tests to the e2e suite to cover tab order, stop shortcut, and toast interactions.

Maya Luo: Thanks! I'll drop the PR link here once it's up. :thumbsup:
